title: register flat cap wrong at real scale
statement: The findings-register length budget applied a flat per-file line cap, so a legitimately large real-scale backlog tripped the hard bound every run. The cap measures finding count rather than prose padding; register-shaped artifacts need a per-entry budget instead.

title: extractor cannot parse prose-shaped artifacts; publish grammars, warn on zero-parse
statement: The metrics extractor parsed zero items from present, non-empty prose-shaped artifacts and reported a silent zero that read as "nothing here". Publish the artifact grammars with conforming examples and warn when a non-empty artifact yields zero parsed items.

title: accepted-by-design checks must read dated decision records
statement: Reviewers repeatedly re-raised deliberate design choices as findings because the accepted-by-design check had no dated decision record to consult. An accepted-by-design verdict must cite a dated ADR or equivalent rather than reviewer memory.

title: refutation panels mandatory at high severity (they killed overstated/harmful fixes)
statement: Refutation panels killed two overstated high-severity findings, one of whose proposed fixes would have been actively harmful. Paneling stays mandatory at high severity; a paneling-coverage metric is the candidate mechanical backstop.

title: executed model identity absent from artifacts; tier substitution invisible
statement: No run artifact recorded which model actually executed a dispatch or led a phase, so a silent tier substitution mid-run left no trace and the tier-mix metric was unreconstructable. Resolved model identity must be stamped into the dispatch ledger per row and per phase.

title: assess-only structurally caps CONFIRMED (DISPROVEN — superseded by L-012)
statement: Recorded as a protocol rule that assess-only runs cannot reach CONFIRMED because operatives cannot execute, so ratios were only comparable within-track. A later run disproved it by reaching CONFIRMED four times through executed proof; superseded by L-012.

title: artifact grammars must be published with conforming examples + zero-parse warning
statement: Extraction only started working after item IDs, tier/severity fields and ledger columns were reshaped by hand, because the expected grammars were never published. Ship the grammars with conforming examples and pair them with a zero-items-in-non-empty-file warning.

title: redaction gate crashes uncaught on a run folder
statement: The redaction gate threw an uncaught error with a non-fail-closed exit code when handed a run folder, which is the invocation its own docs imply. A gate that crashes instead of failing closed silently stops gating.

title: item-ID pattern rejects round letter between hyphen and serial
statement: Findings tagged with a reviewer-round letter between the hyphen and the serial were invisible to both consumers, while unrelated tags in evidence prose were counted instead, so the tool reported a confident number drawn entirely from noise. Widen the pattern and publish conforming and non-conforming examples side by side.

title: item-ID pattern over-matches domain tags in evidence prose
statement: An unanchored item-ID scan counted domain tags appearing inside evidence prose as findings. Item IDs must be matched at entry-heading position only.

title: findings in themed sibling reports invisible to extractor
statement: Findings routed into a themed sibling report never reached any metric, undercounting one run substantially. A sibling artifact carrying register-shaped entries must warn that its findings are not counted.

title: assess-only caps remediation, not reproduction
statement: Assess-only forbids changing the target, not executing against it: findings reached CONFIRMED via repro scripts written outside the target and a failing read-only gate run. The comparison rule is restated as capping remediation rather than reproduction.

title: ledger row must be written atomically with the dispatch call (phantom-row hazard)
statement: A ledger row written a turn before its dispatch call is a phantom row indistinguishable from a hung operative. Write-at-dispatch-time must mean atomically with the call itself.

title: metrics vocabulary cannot distinguish covered negative from failed dispatch
statement: A slice returned a well-formed zero-finding result with every lead traced to a dominating guard, and the metrics reported it identically to a dispatch that failed. The vocabulary needs an explicit covered-negative declaration.

title: The register per-entry length budget has no entry terminator, so trailing covered-negative lines are attributed to the final entry and reliably trip its hard cap
statement: The register per-entry length budget has no entry terminator, so trailing covered-negative lines are attributed to the final entry and reliably trip its hard cap.

title: The refutation log still matches item identifiers mid-line, so explanatory prose citing a finding becomes an unparseable receipt
statement: The refutation log still matches item identifiers mid-line, so explanatory prose citing a finding becomes an unparseable receipt; the entry-heading-position fix applied to registers was never mirrored to refutation logs.

title: The themed-sibling-report warning does not recurse into subdirectories, so per-slice reports carrying entry-shaped findings remain invisible to every register consumer
statement: The themed-sibling-report warning does not recurse into subdirectories, so per-slice reports carrying entry-shaped findings remain invisible to every register consumer.

title: The metrics tool's own output file trips its own sibling-report warning, because the per-entry length lines it emits parse as register entries at line start
statement: The metrics tool's own output file trips its own sibling-report warning, because the per-entry length lines it emits parse as register entries at line start.

title: A ledger row cannot express both that a unit failed and that it was retried, so failed rate and redispatch rate are mutually exclusive for one unit and the pair understates recovery
statement: A ledger row cannot express both that a unit failed and that it was retried, so failed rate and redispatch rate are mutually exclusive for one unit and the pair understates recovery.

title: Operatives label static reasoning as CONFIRMED, so the confirmed ratio measures labelling discipline as much as evidence depth
statement: Operatives label static reasoning as CONFIRMED, so the confirmed ratio measures labelling discipline as much as evidence depth; enforce the tier definition at the operative boundary or add an explicit executed-evidence flag.

title: Persist every operative report to disk in the turn it lands, before any other work
statement: Persist every operative report to disk in the turn it lands, before any other work; four blocked lead turns nearly discarded two high-severity reports that existed only in conversation.

title: A brief that never reaches its operative is indistinguishable at the ledger from a completed dispatch until the report is read, so gate every report on shape before counting the unit covered
statement: A brief that never reaches its operative is indistinguishable at the ledger from a completed dispatch until the report is read, so gate every report on shape before counting the unit covered.

title: The note template prescribes a prose severity-mix shape its own validator rejects as a Unix path, so a note written exactly to template fails closed
statement: The note template prescribes a prose severity-mix shape its own validator rejects as a Unix path, so a note written exactly to template fails closed; reconcile the documented shape with the enforced one.

title: Lens diversity rather than redundancy is what kills a wrong finding: two of three independent readers repeated the same misread of a configuration declaration, and only a differently-lensed panelist caught it
statement: Lens diversity rather than redundancy is what kills a wrong finding: two of three independent readers repeated the same misread of a configuration declaration, and only a differently-lensed panelist caught it.
